title: The constructed scalar tensor comparison preserves the signed interchange
statement: Let X be a scheme, B a finite commutative ring, F the canonical constant-scalar derived equivalence, a an intrinsic tensor-Hom presentation [def-sf-integral-hom-reduction-models], and s its signed representative symmetry [def-sf-integral-verdier-models]. Assume naturality of s.swap in both variables, with the equation of the Lean statement. Let b be a natural isomorphism from the native fixed-scalar curried tensor to its flip, whose components have the HEq normalization by DerivedMonoidal.braiding' used in [lem-weil-duality-pairing]. For the constructed mu of [def-sf-finite-intrinsic-tensor-realization], mu(K,L) followed by F(b(L,K) inverse) equals s.swap(FK,FL) followed by mu(L,K), for every pair K,L. There are no internal-Hom, evaluation, dualizing-object, constructibility or biduality assumptions or conclusions.

source.place: Tags 06YS, 07A4 and 0FPT; sites.tex Tag 00YV. The second paragraph of literature/blueprint/latest/blueprint/sec-smooth-purity/sk-lem-sp-tower/thm-coef-integral-verdier.proof.md, identifying the finite evaluation transpose.

proof.text: Use finiteScalarTensorRepresentativeData_normalization for the restricted intrinsic tensor model. It identifies the constructed mu on termwise flat K-flat representatives with the inverse of finiteScalarTotalTensorIso, conjugated by the exact-functor localization factors and the specified tensor representatives.

The ordinary scalar tensor comparison is normalized on scalar-unit pure sections. Both total-complex interchanges reverse a homogeneous pair (p,q) with coefficient (-1)^(pq). Pure-tensor generation and sheafification adjunction imply equality of chain maps. The representative formula of s and the normalization of b identify their derived images with these signed swaps. Involutivity identifies the inverse b(L,K) with the same interchange in the required direction.

Naturality of mu, the assumed naturality hs of s, and naturality of b express both sides as natural transformations of derived bifunctors. Apply finiteScalarRepresentativesFullyFaithful to the equality on the resolving class. This proves equality on every derived pair, including zero objects and the zero-ring or empty-site cases.

lean.statement:
theorem finiteIntrinsicTensorSymmetry
    (X : Scheme.{u}) (B : Type u) [CommRing B] [Finite B]
    (a : IntegralHom.TensorPresentation.{u, u} X (proEtaleConstantRing X B))
    (s : SignedSymmetry X (proEtaleConstantRing X B) a)
    (hs : ∀ (K L K' L' : proEtaleDerivedCategory X B)
      (f : K ⟶ K') (g : L ⟶ L'),
      a.tensor.map (Prod.mkHom f g) ≫ (s.swap K' L').hom =
        (s.swap K L).hom ≫ a.tensor.map (Prod.mkHom g f))
    (b : CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.curriedTensor
        (DerivedCategory (Sheaf (ProEt.topology X)
          (ModuleCat.{u + 1} (ULift.{u + 1, u} B)))) ≅
      (CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.curriedTensor
        (DerivedCategory (Sheaf (ProEt.topology X)
          (ModuleCat.{u + 1} (ULift.{u + 1, u} B))))).flip)
    (hb : ∀ K L, HEq ((b.hom.app K).app L)
      (DerivedMonoidal.braiding'
        (DerivedCategory.Qh (C := Sheaf (ProEt.topology X)
          (ModuleCat.{u + 1} (ULift.{u + 1, u} B))))
        (HomotopyCategory.quasiIso (Sheaf (ProEt.topology X)
          (ModuleCat.{u + 1} (ULift.{u + 1, u} B))) (.up ℤ)) K L).hom) :
    ∀ K L,
      (finiteIntrinsicTensorRealization X B a).hom.app (K, L) ≫
          (sfIntrinsicDerivedEquivalence X B).functor.map ((b.inv.app L).app K) =
        (s.swap ((sfIntrinsicDerivedEquivalence X B).functor.obj K)
          ((sfIntrinsicDerivedEquivalence X B).functor.obj L)).hom ≫
            (finiteIntrinsicTensorRealization X B a).hom.app (L, K)
